item.title: Claude Dreaming: Managed Agents Memory Stores and Dreams
item.description:
Claude dreaming is an offline memory pass: Claude rereads past session transcripts and its own memory notes, corrects notes that turned out wrong, merges duplicates, and builds new structures such as a wiki or an index that later sessions can navigate. Anthropic described it in The components of agent memory (November 6, 2026) and ships it in Claude Managed Agents as Dreams, a research-preview API.

This page explains what Anthropic means by agent memory, how memory stores and Dreams work, what the published tests showed (CL-Bench, Pokémon Red, a 420M-token wiki), and how the approach compares with Letta’s dreaming and Hindsight’s background consolidation. Every number comes from Anthropic’s post, its docs or its cookbook, and none of it was reproduced here.

item.title: Memory Consolidation in AI Agents: Methods and Results
item.description:
Memory consolidation in AI agents is the step that turns raw records (messages, tool results, observations) into a smaller set of cleaner, longer-lived memories. It merges duplicates, resolves contradictions, and writes higher-level insights. Without it, an agent’s memory store only grows, and retrieval gets noisier with every session.

The term borrows from neuroscience, where consolidation means stabilizing new memories over time. In agents it’s an engineering job, usually done by an LLM in a background process. This page covers the main techniques, when to run them, what goes wrong, and how current systems handle it.
